subject: Q2 Gateway: OKR consolidation, governance sign-off & QBR clearance
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Cc: Julia Park <julia@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 02 May 2028 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: Q2 Gateway: OKR consolidation, governance sign-off & QBR clearance

Team — kicking off a short, focused thread to lock the OKR slate for Q2 and confirm QBR readiness with Acme. Goal is to have final OKRs and the QBR deck cleared for exec review by EOD Thursday so the ops team can schedule rehearsals next week.

Quick context: Acme (pilot customer) has asked for a short product roadmap slice in the QBR deck and to confirm our reliability targets for dedicated deployments. I attached the current OKR draft and the working QBR deck.

Action items I need from this thread: 
- Kim: please review the measurement rubrics in OKR-draft-v3.xlsx and flag any metrics that need reweighting (deadline: Wed 12:00 PT).
- Markus: evaluate SLA and reliability language for the QBR slide and confirm whether we can publish the 99.9% goal for dedicated customers (deadline: Wed 17:00 PT).
- Hannah: run the risk/gap table for governance and call out any compliance blockers for Private deployments (deadline: Wed 17:00 PT).

If we hit those, I will consolidate changes and send the final deck to Julia and Execs on Thursday morning.

Attachments: QBR-deck-v1.pptx (pptx), OKR-draft-v3.xlsx (xlsx), governance-risks-notes.pdf (pdf)

Thanks — Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Head of GTM Programs, Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, markus_klein@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 02 May 2028 10:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Q2 Gateway: OKR consolidation, governance sign-off & QBR clearance

Tessa — thanks for the clear asks. A couple quick notes after a first pass of OKR-draft-v3: 
1) The adoption metric (New dedicated customers onboarded) should be split: New logos vs. Expansion conversions. That will help downstream owners prioritize outreach vs product work.
2) For one of the engineering-facing KPIs (p95 inference latency), suggest we reference the standard test harness (seq length 256, batch 8) so we don't get noisy signals during the QBR.

I'll update the spreadsheet with the splits and a short comment column by Wed noon.

Kimberly
Kimberly Park
VP, Product Ops
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, kimberly_park@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 02 May 2028 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Q2 Gateway: OKR consolidation, governance sign-off & QBR clearance

On Tue, May 2, 2028 at 10:14 AM Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com> wrote:
> I'll update the spreadsheet with the splits and a short comment column by Wed noon.

Good call on the split. Two additional asks from my side:
- For the SLA wording on the QBR slide: we can publish a 99.9% target *as a product goal* but not as an unconditional contractual SLA for Dedicated until we lock the autoscaling SLAs with infra (we have a pending ops ticket). Proposed language: "Reliability target (objective): 99.9% availability for reserved capacity; contractual SLA subject to deployment profile and capacity commitments."
- Please add a one-sentence caveat on quantization and model variants in the product notes slide — it helps set expectations with customers.

I'll paste a suggested slide text below later today.

Markus
Markus Klein
Director, Production Reliability
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, kimberly_park@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 02 May 2028 13:32:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Q2 Gateway: OKR consolidation, governance sign-off & QBR clearance

Looping governance items in — I reviewed governance-risks-notes.pdf and ran a quick gap table:
- Data residency: OK for Hosted + Dedicated in our announced regions; Private (on-prem) needs an explicit runbook for audit evidence (item: audit-log retention policy).
- SOC2 evidence: control mapping looks complete except for one control tied to key lifecycle management where we need KMS proof-of-rotation screenshots.
- Export controls: flagged a potential restriction for the APAC pilot if we include model weights in on-prem bundles.

I'll attach my gap table and add a short mitigation row for each risk in the deck. If we can't close KMS evidence by Friday, we should mark that as an open risk in the QBR notes.

Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Security & Compliance
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Julia Park <julia@acme.com>, kimberly_park@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 02 May 2028 15:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Q2 Gateway: OKR consolidation, governance sign-off & QBR clearance

Julia — looping you in after the team's initial pass. We're consolidating OKRs and locking the final QBR deck for an exec readout on Thursday morning. Highlights for Acme: 
- We will include a short roadmap slide that calls out dedicated deployment reliability goals (product goal: 99.9% availability). Final contractual SLAs will be clarified in the procurement phase.
- We will add a one-line caveat on model quantization/variants so expectations are aligned for latency/cost tradeoffs.
- Hannah is tracking governance gaps (audit logs + KMS rotation screenshots). If we can't close by Friday, we'll surface that as an open item in the QBR notes.

Requested next step: can you confirm whether Acme would like a separate procurement call to discuss deployment SLAs before the QBR? If yes, propose Wed 4:00 PM PT or Thu 9:00 AM PT.

Thanks — Tessa
(Attachment: QBR-deck-v1.pptx; OKR-draft-v3.xlsx)
